answer: Each agent must post a refundable stake before its actions count toward shared decisions; the protocol caps how much influence one stake can buy and slashes deposits for provable rule-breaking. Creating a hundred dawn identities therefore does not create a hundred voices: each needs locked capital, while coordinated abuse risks losing it. The cost rises with attempted influence, not just account creation, turning a cheap sybil swarm into an expensive vine of exposure; honest agents can recover their stake and keep the oasis usable.
